paper.title: Learning to Schedule Online Tasks with Bandit Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Online task scheduling with bandit feedback (reward-to-cost ratio maximization)
unmapped: Each action yields both a random reward and a random positive cost; objective is the ratio of cumulative expected reward to cumulative expected cost
Regret defined as T times |theta* - ratio achieved| (convergence gap), not a standard difference of rewards
Task types (contexts) drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution over S types, each with its own finite decision set A(S)
Learner knows c_min, and theta_min = r_min/c_max, theta_max = r_max/c_min (reward/cost mean ranges)
settings.definition_quote: We assume $S$ types of incoming tasks in the system ... every task is randomly drawn from a stationary probability distribution ... For the $t$th task, the controller observes its type $S_t$ and chooses a decision $a_t \in \mathcal A(S_t)$ ... the controller observes the feedback of reward $R_{S_t,a_t}$ and cost $C_{S_t,a_t}$ ... The controller aims to maximize the cumulative reward-to-cost ratio

conditions: Rewards sub-Gaussian with means in [r_min, r_max]
Costs positive sub-Gaussian with means in [c_min, c_max]
Rewards and costs independent for the same (S,a)

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Suppose Assumption~\ref{assumption:reward} and~\ref{assumption:cost} hold, DOL-RM achieves the following regret: \mathcal{R}(T) = O(T^{\frac{3}{4}}).

results.notes: Regret is R(T) = T * Gap(T), where Gap(T) = |theta* - sum E[R]/sum E[C]| (ratio of expectations), so quantity recorded as 'other'. Equivalent to convergence gap O(T^{-1/4}). Appendix constant C_2 contains sqrt(log T), so the stated O(T^{3/4}) hides a log factor; also the proof assumes each (S,a) explored once beforehand.

cited_results.setting_description: Online task scheduling reward-to-cost ratio maximization with perfectly known rewards and costs (only task arrival distribution unknown)
